layout_note: Opening page of a lectionary INDEX table: 'A TABLE OF THE EPISTLES TAKEN FORTH OF THE OLD TESTAMENT, vpon certayne feſtitual dayes.' The whole page sits inside a double-ruled rectangular frame with a band of printer's-flower ornaments below the top-left page number (1018) and above the display title. STRUCTURE: this is a SINGLE full-width column of entries read straight top-to-bottom (NOT two side-by-side columns of entries). The 'columnar' character is WITHIN each row: every row is a two-field record pairing a FEAST / OCCASION label (left, roman upright type) with its SCRIPTURE REFERENCE (right, italic) — e.g. 'S. Iohn Euangeliſt. | Eccli. 15. v. 1. to v. 7.'. Reference syntax = book-abbreviation + chapter + verse range ('v. X. to v. Y.', or 'to Y', or 'to the end', or '& ca. Z' for a second chapter, '& v.' for an extra verse). Two exceptions: line_index 15 ('S. Iohn ante portam Latinam, the ſame.') gives a cross-reference 'the ſame.' instead of a citation; line_index 28 (the Anniversary of the dead) is set ENTIRELY in italic. The reference range-connector is set in an italic sort that renders almost identically to the numeral '10'; it is the WORD 'to' (proved by the fully spelled-out 'to the end' / 'to the v.' forms) and is transcribed 'to' throughout. GLYPH REGIMES: roman occasions/rubric and italic references BOTH use a real single 'w' sort (e.g. 'new', 'Mathew') — there is NO 'vv' anywhere on this page. long-ſ is glyph-driven. The page is heavily FOXED (many raised ink dots); several dots read like stray points, so exact period placement inside references is approximate. Foot-of-page right-justified quire signature 'NA' (binder's mark). No true catchword.

uncertain.note: High-zoom (7x) reading is f-e-ſt(ligature)-i-t-u-a-l = 'feſtitual', a compositor typo for 'feſtiual' (festival) with an intrusive 't'. Preserved as printed per diplomatic rule.
Clear at 5x: B-o-p-t-i-ſ-t = 'Boptiſt', a typo for 'Baptiſt' (o set for a). The correct 'Baptiſt' is printed at line_index 22 on this same page. Preserved as printed.

The italic range-connector between '10' and '15' renders almost identically to the numeral '10'. Read as the word 'to' by table-wide consistency and by the spelled-out 'to the end' forms elsewhere. Applies to every 'to' in the reference column.
The ascender after 'Ceci' read as 'l' (St Cecilia = 'Cecilie'); at ~180 DPI the l is faintly separable from a long-ſ, but 'l' fits the name and the stroke shows no long-ſ nub.
Abbreviation worn on this line; transcribed 'Eccli.' to match the clearly-set 'Eccli.' at line_index 26. A colon-like terminal ('Eccl:') is possible but judged worn 'i.'.

Page-wide: heavy foxing produces many raised dots; the exact number and placement of periods inside the italic references (e.g. 'v. 1. to v. 7.') is approximate. Numerals themselves were zoom-verified; interstitial points were not all individually adjudicated.

glyph_counts.note: recompute long_s by counting U+017F in body[].text. w/vv: page has real 'w' only (roman + italic), zero 'vv'.

method: visual-multimodal read of the ~180 DPI raster (diag-reocr/newmode-jp2/lectionary-table.png, source S6), read region-by-region with 3-7x LANCZOS word-level zoom on every line and targeted zooms on the title word 'feſtitual', 'Boptiſt', 'Magdelen', 'Mathew', 'Cecilie'/'Catherin', the final italic line and the foot signature; structural model = ground-truth/matter-nt-table.json (two-field tabular GT). No external text used as a spelling oracle; janvier/DR consulted only as a content sanity-check on which feast maps to which reference.
confidence: Medium-high overall. HIGH on the roman occasion labels and on long-ſ/u-v/i-j decisions (word-level zoom on every line; page has real 'w' only, zero 'vv'). MEDIUM on the italic reference column: the range-connector renders like the numeral '10' and is transcribed 'to' by consistency + sense, and heavy foxing makes exact period placement approximate (numerals were zoom-verified). Preserved typos: 'feſtitual' (subtitle, for feſtiual) and 'Boptiſt' (line 16, for Baptiſt). 'Magdelen', 'Cecilie', 'Catherin', 'Mathew' verified as printed. Lower certainty on the smallest worn italic marks (e.g. line 27 'Eccli.') at ~180 DPI.
